subject: Biotechnology
title: Bioleaching of E-Waste
description: A short lesson to help you apply Bioleaching of E-Waste.

hook.text: A ton of circuit boards contains 40 times more gold than a ton of ore — bacteria can extract those metals without toxic chemicals.

buildup.text: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans produces sulfuric acid — dissolving copper, zinc, and nickel from electronic waste at room temp.

discovery.text: Bioleaching recovers 98% of copper from low-grade ores — mining companies already use bacteria on an industrial scale.

twist.text: E-waste bioleaching is slower than smelting — processing takes days instead of hours, limiting commercial adoption.

climax.text: Cyanide-producing bacteria selectively dissolve gold from circuit boards — a biological alternative to toxic e-waste smelting.

punchline.text: Bacteria mine your old phone — bioleaching recovers precious metals from electronic waste.

quiz.question: How do Acidithiobacillus bacteria extract metals from electronic waste?
options: They absorb metals directly into their cell walls
They produce sulfuric acid that dissolves copper, zinc, and nickel from circuit boards at room temperature
They convert metals into gaseous forms that can be collected

details.summary: Bioleaching uses acidophilic bacteria and fungi to extract valuable metals from electronic waste by dissolving them into solution. Organisms like Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans produce acids and oxidants that liberate copper, gold, and rare earth elements from circuit boards and components.
details.whyItMatters: Electronic waste contains more gold per ton than gold ore, yet most is landfilled or processed with toxic chemicals. Bioleaching offers an environmentally friendly alternative for urban mining, recovering critical metals while avoiding harsh
takeaways: Bacteria dissolve metals from electronic waste through acid and oxidant production
Bioleaching recovers copper, gold, and rare earth elements from circuit boards
The process is cheaper and cleaner than conventional chemical metal extraction

faq.question: How do bacteria extract gold from electronic waste?
faq.answer: Bacteria like Chromobacterium violaceum produce cyanide that dissolves gold from circuit board surfaces. Acidithiobacillus species generate sulfuric acid that leaches copper and other base metals. The dissolved metals are then recovered from solution using conventional metallurgical techniques.

faq.question: Is bioleaching fast enough for industrial e-waste recycling?
faq.answer: Bioleaching is slower than chemical processing, taking days to weeks versus hours. However, its lower cost, reduced toxicity, and lower energy requirements compensate. Hybrid approaches combining biological pre-treatment with faster chemical steps are being developed for industrial scale.
